Dear Tamsin,

Thank you for the call last week and for sending the facilities report so promptly. I am writing to pull together the loose ends on our three pictures before the holidays, so that our shipping people and yours are working from the same page.

Crates. Our crate builder in Long Island City will build new crates for all three works to the specification in your facilities report: double-walled, foam-lined, with the inner travel frames for the two Merrins. The external dimensions will follow from their workshop by the middle of December; I have asked them to keep each crate under the height of your goods lift, which I understand is 2.4 metres. Each crate will carry a shock indicator and a tilt indicator, and the condition reports will travel in a sealed sleeve on the outside of the crate.

Climate. We understand the galleries run at 50 per cent relative humidity, plus or minus five, and 19 to 21 degrees. That suits the panels and the canvases alike. Please could you let us know whether the crates may rest unopened for the usual 24 hours once they arrive, as our insurers prefer?

Certificates. Our insurers ask that the certificate of insurance names Carrow & Webb as loss payee and runs nail to nail. Your broker's draft wording looked right to us, but I have copied our registrar in case anything needs tightening before it is issued.

Photography and credits. You are welcome to photograph all three works for the catalogue, the press pack and the website. The credit line should read 'Courtesy of Carrow & Webb Gallery, New York' in every case.

Values. We will confirm the agreed values separately; nothing in this note changes them.

Shipping. Our shippers will deliver the crates to JFK for the flight your agent books; we understand Northwold will handle the export side here. We would like to be told the flight number as soon as it is fixed so that our own courier list can be closed.

Catalogue. Many thanks for the draft entries. A few small corrections to dates and provenance are marked on the attached proof; nothing that affects the loan itself.

With best wishes for the exhibition,

Daniel Carrow
Carrow & Webb Gallery, New York

messages.text: Welcome back, everyone. Staff sync moves to 9:30 Mondays starting this week.
Noted - I will update the shared calendar invite.
Anniversary lecture series: three speakers confirmed for spring. Holding the hall for the second Thursdays.
I will draft the member announcement once the third date locks.
Roof assessment for the Bull Street property is back - repairs scoped under the restoration grant. Summary in the drive.
Actuals are tracking within the grant line. I flagged the January drawdown for the finance review.
Docent orientation is Saturday at 9. Amos is leading the Friday walking tour this month.
December close is done - statement of activities posted for Thursday's review with Reginald.
Put all four Dutch dealer pictures on one van. Splitting the Amsterdam consignment doubles the courier cost for nothing.
Use Bryony's market rates for the euro and krona values, they're the latest we have.
Aldred are a museum, so their two go under the indemnity like the other museums.
Couriers by seniority this time, surely. Hollis should take the big Swedish loan.
Keel & Lantern's premium is 0.18% flat, same as last year.
I'm off 22-26 February, I've put in for it, so leave me off those trips.
Garside's agreement is as good as signed, count their two pictures in.
The Carrow & Webb values are as in their agreement, nothing's changed there.
The 2027 rate schedule is out, use that for the premium, it's cheaper.
Please don't post figures in here; I'll take them from the note.
All the condition checks are done now.
The Strandhuis van comes on the 12th as booked.
Fire alarm test Thursday 10:00 as usual.

pages.title: Brennock Museum staff handbook
pages.body: Start here. The pages below cover the building, front of house and the people side of working at the museum.

pages.title: Opening and closing the building
pages.body: The duty manager opens the staff entrance at 08:30, sets the galleries' lights at 09:45 and does the closing sweep from 16:45, galleries first, toilets last.

pages.title: Visitor emergencies and first aid
pages.body: Radio the duty manager first. First aiders are listed on the board behind the front desk; the defibrillator is in the foyer by the lift.

pages.title: Lost children and lost property
pages.body: A lost child stays at the front desk with two members of staff. Lost property is logged in the blue book and kept for 30 days.

pages.title: Fire evacuation
pages.body: The assembly point is the far side of Quay Road by the war memorial. Gallery staff sweep their gallery and report to the duty manager at the assembly point.

pages.title: Cash handling at the front desk and shop
pages.body: Floats are counted in pairs at opening and closing. Card refunds over twenty pounds need the retail manager or the duty manager.

pages.title: Working with volunteers
pages.body: Volunteers sign in on the tablet at the staff entrance. Their rota is on the volunteers' noticeboard; please tell Fenella about any change of shift.

pages.title: Room hire: setting up the lecture theatre
pages.body: Chairs for 120 are stacked in the store behind the stage. Hirers' caterers use the cafe kitchen only with the cafe manager present.

pages.title: IT: printing, Wi-Fi and passwords
pages.body: Staff Wi-Fi is BMAG-Staff; visitors use BMAG-Guest. Passwords change every 90 days; raise a ticket in the IT helpdesk if you are locked out.

pages.title: Photography and filming requests
pages.body: Commercial filming needs a signed location agreement from the marketing office. Visitors may take photos for personal use without flash.

pages.title: Christmas opening hours 2026
pages.body: Open as normal until 23 December, 10:00 to 13:00 on Christmas Eve, closed 25 and 26 December and 1 January.

pages.title: Staff Christmas lunch
pages.body: Friday 18 December at 13:00 in the cafe, volunteers welcome. Menu choices to Fenella by 4 December.

pages.title: Tidelines: pre-loan condition checks
pages.body: One comment per lender visit records the outcome of the pre-loan condition check for each object.
